title: How a nuclear power plant works (built from blocks)

lines.text: This is how a nuclear power plant works, built out of blocks.
It all starts with a uranium pellet about the size of your thumbnail.
That one tiny pellet holds as much energy as a ton of coal.
Pellets are stacked into fuel rods, and the rods are packed into the reactor core.
When a uranium atom splits, it gives off heat and more neutrons, which split even more atoms.
Control rods slide in to soak up those neutrons and keep the reaction steady.
The heat goes into water that's kept under pressure, so it can't boil.
That hot water boils a second loop of water into steam.
The steam blasts through a turbine and spins it, and the turbine turns a generator that makes electricity.
Then the steam is cooled back into water and pumped around again.
And those giant towers? That's just water vapor. Not smoke.
Would you live next to one?
